full_judgment: 10. In the instant case it is found that the pre-emptor at first filed the case under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and the deposit was made of the consideration money and 5% of the same compensation. After conversion of the case under section 96 of the State' Acquisition find Tenancy Act the defect was detected as to deposit of balance of 5% of the compensation. The balance amount was deposited as per order of the trial Court granting amendment application and as such, deposit can be treated and accepted as valid deposit which was made after the amendment of the pre-emption application and the amendment since relates back to the date of filing of the pre-emption case which was made in time, the case, is not barred by limitation. In the case of Md Mofizuddin Sarker vs Md Abdul Jabbar Akhand, reported in 1 BLD 486 which is a Single Bench decision, it has been held that if the application is made within the period of limitation and the consideration money is also deposited in court within the period of limitation, it shall be deemed that the deposit has been made while making the application for pre-emption under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (XXVIII) of 1951 s 96(3 ) (a) (para 2) So the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, wherein it has been stated that the deposit of the consideration money along with 10% compensation shall accompany the pre-emption, application, in view of the said decision. I find that the time for deposit has been relaxed and extended. So the principle as to deposit is not rigid and it is not mandatory that the entire deposit both the consideration money and compensation should be paid before filing of the case. Moreover, in the instant case the deposit of consideration money along with 5% of the compensation was made in time and it accompanied the petition of pre-emption. Only balance of 5% compensation was deposited after amendment.
